title: OpenAI's Enterprise Revenue Overtakes Consumer for the First Time, CFO Tells Investors
excerpt: Sarah Friar reveals that business customers now generate more revenue than ChatGPT's consumer subscriptions, marking a pivotal shift in OpenAI's path to profitability.
body:
• OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told investors that the company's enterprise business now generates more revenue than its consumer segment, crossing a milestone projected for late 2026.
  • Enterprise revenue has climbed from 20% of total sales when Friar joined in 2024 to over 50% today, driven by aggressive corporate adoption of ChatGPT and API integrations.
  • The shift comes as OpenAI faces intensifying competition from Anthropic, whose Claude platform has gained significant traction among enterprise customers and software developers.
  • OpenAI has shed consumer initiatives including the Sora video generator to focus compute resources on business-grade AI products.

A Revenue Milestone

OpenAI's enterprise business has officially overtaken its consumer segment in revenue, Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar told investors on Thursday, crossing a milestone the company had projected for the end of 2026.

https://x.com/AIPulseNewsX/status/2088356716568055892

The landmark shift caps a rapid transformation. When Friar joined as CFO in 2024, business customers accounted for roughly 20% of OpenAI's revenue. That figure climbed to 40% earlier this year and has now pushed past the halfway mark, according to Friar's remarks reported by CNBC.

OpenAI's revenue run rate has topped $40 billion, fueled by explosive growth in enterprise API usage. The company's APIs now process over 15 billion tokens per minute, while Codex, its coding agent, serves more than 2 million weekly users with month-over-month growth exceeding 70%.

"You'll see a new model coming from us in short order. We feel very excited about it."

— Sarah Friar, CFO, OpenAI

From Consumer Darling to Enterprise Platform

The crossover marks a fundamental reorientation for a company that built its brand on ChatGPT's viral consumer adoption. OpenAI still boasts more than 900 million weekly users of its core product, but Friar has acknowledged that about 95% of them pay nothing.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=oWUr4DKLWZ0

That reality has forced difficult choices. OpenAI shuttered its Sora video generator app and shelved plans for ChatGPT erotica features, redirecting compute resources toward business-grade AI products. The company also hired Slack CEO Denise Dresser as its first chief revenue officer three months ago, tasking her with landing enterprise accounts.

"Tech companies, when they're growing, it's just this natural thing that happens. There's so many cool things you could do," Friar told the Associated Press. "Great companies are very good at that winnowing down and refocusing, and it's super painful."

The Anthropic Factor

The enterprise pivot carries added urgency because of Anthropic. The rival AI lab, valued at $380 billion, has carved out a strong position among corporate customers and software developers with its Claude platform. Enterprise customers account for roughly 80% of Anthropic's business, according to CEO Dario Amodei.

Anthropic recently claimed its annualized revenue had reached $30 billion — a figure OpenAI's leadership has challenged, arguing it doesn't account for revenue Anthropic shares with cloud partners Amazon and Google.

"They're likely quite close," said Luke Emberson, a researcher at nonprofit Epoch AI. "Certainly the trends show Anthropic is growing much faster than OpenAI. If that continues, they're likely to cross soon."

"It's really clear to me that companies are past the experimentation phase and they're into using AI to do real work."

— Denise Dresser, Chief Revenue Officer, OpenAI

New Models, New Strategy

OpenAI is preparing to launch a new model codenamed Spud, which it describes as its "smartest model yet" with stronger reasoning and more reliable production output. The company also recently released GPT-Rosalind, a specialized model for drug discovery and life sciences research.

The enterprise push is backed by a $122 billion funding round and partnerships with Microsoft, Oracle, AWS, NVIDIA, and AMD. Friar has indicated the company will not reach cash-flow positive status before 2028, even as annualized cash burn has climbed past $15 billion.

What to Watch

The revenue crossover signals a maturing business model, but it also raises questions about the sustainability of the AI industry's spending trajectory. Both OpenAI and Anthropic lose more money than they earn, and skeptics warn that startups building on their platforms face risk as the companies optimize for profitability.

"People will say, 'Once they go public, they're safe.' That's not true," said AI critic Ed Zitron. "Public companies can and will die, especially ones that are dependent on $100 billion to $200 billion every year, just to keep breathing."
